correctness.rationale: For rank-one square-zero A=uφ, B=vψ, AB=BA cannot be nonzero, as equality of two nonzero pure tensors forces A and B proportional, contradicting A²=0. Any clique has image-span W annihilated by every vertex, hence lies in C_W. Conversely every C_W is a clique, is inclusion-maximal by testing all u in W and all φ in W⊥, and its image-span recovers W uniquely. Counting rank-one maps by their image lines yields [r]_q(q^{n-r}-1). The maximum follows from minimization of q^r+q^{n-r}; Möbius inversion on the subspace lattice counts ordered tuples with exactly prescribed image-span, and division by k! counts each unordered clique exactly once. All quantifiers, dimension boundaries, and zero matrix exclusion are explicit. The actual attached standard-library checker independently constructs complete adjacency and all maximal cliques, matches five finite cases, and verifies k-clique counts through k=4. Finite tests do not prove the general formula.

value.rationale: Classifying maximal cliques and all smaller clique counts of a natural conjugacy-invariant matrix commuting graph is a motivated structural problem. The result turns the graph into explicit finite Grassmannian incidence data, determines sharp clique numbers, all maximal clique sizes and vertex-clique incidences, and resolves overlap among maximal cliques by a full Möbius-inversion clique polynomial for every n and q. It is not merely a small-case table or a renaming of an existing formula; it gives the entire infinite-parameter invariant.
